bull_bear.body: Historically paid 50% of profits as dividends; currently under internal review for policy update — no concrete decision yet; cash reserves available for inorganic plays but no active targets; acquisition interest exists but scale of targets too small to justify cost
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: High rental inflation in tier-2 cities delaying store openings; reliance on wedding-centric demand; potential GST volatility; competition from regional players entering/exiting cycle; no quick-commerce integration due to third-party warehouse model
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, and long-term oriented; emphasis on SSG over store count; proud of marketing ROI (1B+ views for Made for Each Other); transparent on GST distortion; cautious on capex due to rental environment; open to acquisitions but no active pipeline
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 1. 85% higher revenue/sq ft in new vs closed stores — indicates superior location selection, not just size; 2. Twamev’s 18-20 month lead time means current signings are for FY28/FY29 openings; 3. Diwas digital sales are scaling but inventory cannot be used by Zilo/Blinkit — company may need to build its own logistics; 4. 5-6% of retail area is underperforming — higher than typical 2-3%, signaling aggressive rationalization underway
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Asset-light, franchisee-led EBO distribution model with high cash conversion ratio is the stated capital model; the deck cites 'Strong growth trajectory with industry leading margins, return metrics & healthy cash generation'.
- RoCE (Pre-Tax) series shown for FY22 to FY26: 75.38%, 95.32%, 85.27%, 68.69%, 63.09% (RoCE numerator and denominator definitions are given in the deck's own footnote).
- 'Disciplined approach towards acquisitions' is listed as one of five growth-strategy pillars; the only acquisition disclosed is the strategic acquisition of Mebaz (brand started 2002, acquired by the company in 2017).
- Kedaara Capital invested during the pre-listing period per the evolution timeline, followed by listing on stock exchanges.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Market-leader in the Indian celebration wear segment with a diverse portfolio of brands catering to the aspirations of the entire family
- Large and growing Indian wedding and celebration wear market driven by increased customer spending on such wear
- Omni-channel network with the seamless integration of offline and online channels
- Differentiated business model combining the strengths of retailing with branded consumer play
- Technology-based strong supply chain and inventory replenishment systems driven by system-wide data analytics, strong processes, and long-standing vendor relationships
- Experienced and professional founder-led leadership team
- No end of season sales or discounts for the Manyavar brand
- Continued investment in capturing consumer taste preferences at a pin code level, enabling hyper-local demand sensing for sharper inventory planning and reduced markdowns
- The Company is debt-free, with negligible interest rate risk from financial liabilities
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Category and occasion concentration in Indian wedding and celebration wear — Management states the industry may face challenges due to high concentration on Indian wedding and celebration wear and is vulnerable to variations in demand; revenue is tied to a single discretionary occasion category, and BRSR reports 100% of turnover from Wearing Apparel & Accessories.
- Shifting consumer preferences and fashion cycles — Management explicitly flags vulnerability to changes in consumer preferences; the Company's response has been to reinvent core products for Gen Z, reposition Mohey and Mebaz, and invest in pin-code-level demand sensing to reduce markdowns.
- Intensifying competition in the organised celebration wear market — Management notes the market has increasing participation and competition and that other players falling under the same industry may increase competition, pressuring the Company's market-leading position and its no-discount stance on Manyavar.
- Commodity / raw material price risk — The Company states it is affected by price volatility of its key raw materials and traded goods, with operating activities requiring a continuous supply of key material; the procurement department monitors price fluctuation to minimise exposure. The primary market risk to the Company is commodity price risk.
- Credit risk concentrated in trade receivables from franchisees and distribution partners — The maximum exposure to credit risk is primarily from trade receivables; the Company manages it through security deposits and bank guarantees from customers, credit approvals, credit limits and continuous monitoring of customer creditworthiness, with an impairment analysis performed at each reporting date.
- Foreign exchange risk on overseas sales — The Company operates in domestic and international markets and is exposed to foreign exchange risk through sales in overseas countries, principally USD with smaller CAD and GBP exposure; it holds forward contracts to mitigate the risk of changes in exchange rates.
- Investment price risk on treasury portfolio — The Company has invested in bonds, debentures and mutual funds which are susceptible to market price risk arising from changes in interest rates or market yields that may impact the return and value of such investments; it manages this by diversifying the portfolio.
- Dependence on attracting and retaining skilled personnel — The Company states its continued growth depends on the ability to attract, hire, train and retain skilled personnel — a structural exposure for a retail organisation whose in-store experience is a core differentiator.
- Supply chain fragmentation in the apparel sector — The Company notes the apparel sector supply chain is largely unorganised and fragmented and that it works with a diverse network of suppliers for raw materials, accessories and finished goods, creating dependence on jobbers and third-party vendors for quality and compliance.
- Regulatory and product-labelling compliance — The BRSR discloses a non-monetary regulatory instance concerning information not provided on the product label as required by law, which caused violation of Rule 9 of Legal Metrology Packaged Commodities Rule 2011.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Manyavar: core brand, 669 stores; Mohey: 8 standalone EBOs, higher ASP than Manyavar; Twamev: 8 standalone EBOs, highest revenue/sq ft, build-to-suit stores with 18-20 month lead time; Mebaz: focused on wedding/occasion wear; Diwas: digital-only, no physical stores planned; combined Manyavar-Mohey stores: all upgraded, no retrofitting possible
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Described as the largest company in India in men's Indian wedding & celebration wear by Revenue, OPBDIT and PAT, commanding a dominant position in a conventionally unorganized market (source: Crisil Report, as of FY20, latest available).
- Manyavar is stated to be the category leader in the branded Indian wedding & celebration wear market with pan-India presence; Mohey is stated to be the largest brand by number of stores in women's Indian wedding & celebration wear with pan-India presence (both sourced to the Crisil Report, as of FY20).
- 'Aspirational Yet Value for Money': uniform pricing across online and offline channels in India, and no discounts / end-of-season sales for the Manyavar brand.
- 'Having First mover advantage, VFL scaled up and organized highly unorganized and fragmented category'; the deck claims a 'Multi Decade growth Opportunity for the Category from here'.
- Positioned as a one-stop destination for men, women and kids across all celebratory occasions and price points, delivered through an omni-channel network of EBOs, MBOs, LFS and Online (own website and leading lateral e-commerce platforms).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Marketing / brand assets] The deck details campaign activity including the Manyavar-Mohey 'Made for Each Other' campaign featuring Rashmika and Vijay, Vijay Devarakonda AI content, a Safari x Manyavar collaboration, Mohey influencer and stylist activations, Twamev's 'Truly You' / 'Product Is King' storytelling with Nupur Sanon, and Diwas festive content; the company has been Official Sponsor of 2 IPL teams and Official Indian Wear Partner of 3 IPL teams, and Celebration Wear Partner in Femina Miss India 2021.
- [Founder / heritage] Headquartered in Kolkata and incorporated in 2002 by Mr. Ravi Modi; the Manyavar brand started operations via a predecessor entity in 1999, with the first EBO in Bhubaneshwar.
- [Data vintage caveat] All market-leadership claims are sourced to the Crisil Report dated Sep-2021 as updated by an addendum dated December 2021, with the positioning statistics marked 'As of FY20 (latest available)'.
- [Metric definitions] The deck's 'Sales of Customers' / 'Retail Sales' is a distinct measure from Revenue from Operations - it comprises sales of the company's brands made by its EBOs, LFSs and online channel customers, plus sales made by the company to MBOs (including shop-in-shops) and certain lateral e-commerce platform customers at RSP - and must not be read as company revenue.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Vedant Fashions Limited, incorporated in 2002 and headquartered in Kolkata, is primarily engaged in manufacturing, trading and sale of readymade ethnic wear for men, women and kids, primarily in India, under the brand names Manyavar, Mohey, Mebaz, Twamev and Diwas. It caters to a diverse consumer base seeking ready-to-wear ethnic and occasion-based apparel and accessories for traditional, wedding, festive and celebration wear occasions. The Company follows an omni-channel retail strategy, serving customers through exclusive brand outlets (EBOs), multi-brand outlets (MBOs), large format stores (LFS) and digital platforms including its own website and leading third-party e-commerce portals.

business.body:
- **Wearing Apparel & Accessories:** Manyavar, Mohey, Twamev, Diwas, Mebaz
- **Men's celebration wear:** Manyavar, Jodhpuri, footwear and men's accessories
- **Women's celebration wear:** Mohey, ready-to-wear and drape-led occasion wear, bags and clutches
- **Premium / luxury:** Twamev, EverAfter, The Drop, The Chord, Twilight Gala
- **Festive / Gen-Z:** Diwas
- **Regional (Southern market):** Mebaz

business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin held at 65.7% (FY) despite 150 bps contraction — primarily due to GST rate normalization (not input inflation); fabric cost impact estimated at INR 1-1.5 per INR 100 MRP product, absorbed via SKU upgradation, not price hikes; no margin pressure from franchisees
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: no explicit guidance, but confidence in sustained SSG momentum; margin: gross margin to remain ~65%+ despite 50-150 bps input cost inflation; order inflow: no specific guidance; capex/commissioning: no capex guidance, but Twamev EBOs have 18-20 month lead time for openings
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion into high-throughput neighborhoods with 1,000 sq ft Manyavar kurta-only stores; potential for own quick-commerce app/dark hubs; untapped markets like South Bombay (Lower Parel+); new India tier-2 cities (e.g., Bhopal) with high rental friction
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Shift the product architecture from category breadth to category depth, making offerings resonate with the evolving preferences of younger consumers — exemplified by reinventing the iconic Jodhpuri with comfort engineering and contemporary occasion-wear sensibilities to appeal to the Gen Z consumer
- Deepen regional relevance by developing occasion-specific and fabric-led offerings tailored to distinct cultural preferences and local traditions in key regional markets
- Reposition Mohey from a bridal wear brand to a broader wedding wear brand encompassing the full spectrum of celebration occasions, and deepen this strategy in the current financial year
- Reposition Mebaz from a wedding-only player to an all-season, all-occasion celebration wear destination under the brand idea 'Celebrations Begin with Mebaz', broadening its addressable base beyond the wedding season in its core Southern market
- Extend Twamev's luxury positioning through the 'Truly You' proposition and a 'Product Is King' storytelling approach, expanding into contemporary casual-formal hybrids and experiential events
- Build Diwas as a festive-first, Gen-Z brand through sustained presence on marketplaces and quick-commerce platforms, deepening quick commerce and B2B partnerships
- Full-scale activation of omnichannel capabilities so online orders are fulfilled through the store network, expanding product availability and enabling faster deliveries
- Invest in e-commerce platform UI/UX, AI-led product discovery and personalised recommendations, streamlined one-click checkout and cart-recovery mechanisms to lift conversion and e-commerce revenue contribution
- Embed AI across the organisation — AI-powered training content on the VFL Parivaar learning platform, Claude Enterprise deployed organisation-wide, AI-driven intelligence in real estate site selection, and AI-enabled in-store cameras for footfall and conversion capture
- Scale the digitally enabled in-store alteration process into a fully automated, standardised end-to-end post-purchase experience
- Deepen the women's wear offering in ready-to-wear and drape-led segments, complemented by an expanded accessories range including bags and clutches
- Sustain brand-building through integrated marketing — owned intellectual property, celebrity partnerships, influencer programmes, outdoor activations, digital storytelling and retail theatre — across every brand
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Vedant Fashions is an asset-light, franchisee-led retailer whose expansion is measured in retail footprint rather than plant capacity. As on March 31, FY26 the total retail footprint stood at 1.79 million sq. ft., and the Exclusive Brand Outlet (EBO) area — the dominant channel — spanned 669 stores (including SIS) in 252 cities and towns globally, of which the national EBO tally was 652 stores (including SIS) across 240 cities and towns in India. During the year the Company expanded brand presence by launching one exclusive brand outlet for the Twamev brand of 9,000 sq ft. Operationally the Company runs a centralized warehouse at Dhulagarh, Howrah, West Bengal, its registered and corporate office at Paridhan Garment Park, Kolkata, and fifteen company-operated retail outlets (five in Kolkata, two in Mumbai, eight in Bangalore); BRSR reports 16 plants and 1 office nationally and none internationally. International presence spans stores in five countries — USA, UAE, UK, Canada and Australia. Capacity-style investment during the year was directed at capability rather than manufacturing lines: full-scale activation of omnichannel fulfilment enabling online orders to be served from the store network, significant investment in brand-website UI/UX and AI-led product discovery, a performance-based allocation framework for logistics partners, scaling of AI-enabled camera infrastructure to an increased number of stores for footfall and conversion capture, organisation-wide deployment of Claude Enterprise, AI-driven intelligence embedded in real estate site selection and expansion decisions, and full automation of the in-store alteration workflow.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's young demographic profile sustaining a large and aspirational consumer base with a strong propensity for fashion spending
- Accelerating urbanization expanding the addressable market and reshaping consumption patterns across Tier II and Tier III cities
- Rising participation of women in the workforce driving incremental demand for formal and occasion-specific apparel categories
- A gradual but decisive shift in consumer preference from unbranded to Ready-Made Garments (RMG), elevating market quality and value
- Deeper penetration of organized and branded players reinforcing consumer trust, standardizing sizing and quality expectations, and widening market formalization
- Expanding physical retail infrastructure alongside rapidly growing e-commerce adoption improving product accessibility and convenience
- Growing consumer awareness of fashion trends driven by social media influence and global exposure, shortening purchase cycles and elevating aspirational spending
- The increasing trend of multi-day wedding functions in India and higher spending per consumer, with demand driven not only by the immediate family of the bride and groom but also their close friends
- Frequent festivities in India driving the wedding and celebration wear category
- The E-commerce channel delivered robust growth during the year, while the relatively newer brands Twamev, Diwas and Mohey together recorded strong overall growth, strengthening overall brand portfolio performance
- Mohey's repositioning to a broader wedding wear brand has yielded encouraging early results, reflected in improved store footfalls and stronger floor conversions
- The Directors remain optimistic that the integrated and culturally attuned approach — spanning digital commerce, customer engagement, data analytics and AI-assisted tools — will continue to attract new customers, deepen loyalty and strengthen brand equity, supporting long-term growth
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Vedant Fashions delivered robust Q4FY26 retail sales growth of 7.8% and PAT growth of 13%, driven by record-breaking marketing campaigns and disciplined SSG improvement of 2.7% for FY26; the company is shifting from volume-led expansion to quality-led retail, prioritizing higher ASP via product upgradation and rationalizing underperforming stores, while sustaining industry-leading 65%+ gross margins despite GST normalization headwinds.

open.horizon: FY26 final dividend, subject to approval at AGM on September 28, 2026
open.item: The Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 7.75 per equity share of INR 1 each fully paid-up for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM.
The Company is deepening Mohey's repositioning from bridal wear to a broader wedding wear brand covering the full spectrum of celebration occasions in the current financial year.
The Company will deepen Mohey's repositioning from bridal wear to a broader wedding wear brand covering the full spectrum of celebration occasions in the current financial year.
The Company remains committed to leveraging technology, data and omnichannel integration to deliver a seamless and reliable digital commerce experience.

Management flags that the industry may face challenges from high concentration on Indian wedding and celebration wear, vulnerability to variations in demand and changes in consumer preferences, and increasing competition.
The Company has integrated AI-driven intelligence into its real estate strategy to make sharper, data-driven site selection and expansion decisions.

currentContext.expansion: Vedant Fashions is an asset-light, franchisee-led retailer whose expansion is measured in retail footprint rather than plant capacity. As on March 31, FY26 the total retail footprint stood at 1.79 million sq. ft., and the Exclusive Brand Outlet (EBO) area — the dominant channel — spanned 669 stores (including SIS) in 252 cities and towns globally, of which the national EBO tally was 652 stores (including SIS) across 240 cities and towns in India. During the year the Company expanded brand presence by launching one exclusive brand outlet for the Twamev brand of 9,000 sq ft. Operationally the Company runs a centralized warehouse at Dhulagarh, Howrah, West Bengal, its registered and corporate office at Paridhan Garment Park, Kolkata, and fifteen company-operated retail outlets (five in Kolkata, two in Mumbai, eight in Bangalore); BRSR reports 16 plants and 1 office nationally and none internationally. International presence spans stores in five countries — USA, UAE, UK, Canada and Australia. Capacity-style investment during the year was directed at capability rather than manufacturing lines: full-scale activation of omnichannel fulfilment enabling online orders to be served from the store network, significant investment in brand-website UI/UX and AI-led product discovery, a performance-based allocation framework for logistics partners, scaling of AI-enabled camera infrastructure to an increased number of stores for footfall and conversion capture, organisation-wide deployment of Claude Enterprise, AI-driven intelligence embedded in real estate site selection and expansion decisions, and full automation of the in-store alteration workflow.

risks.risk: Category and occasion concentration in Indian wedding and celebration wear
risks.note: Management states the industry may face challenges due to high concentration on Indian wedding and celebration wear and is vulnerable to variations in demand; revenue is tied to a single discretionary occasion category, and BRSR reports 100% of turnover from Wearing Apparel & Accessories.

risks.risk: Shifting consumer preferences and fashion cycles
risks.note: Management explicitly flags vulnerability to changes in consumer preferences; the Company's response has been to reinvent core products for Gen Z, reposition Mohey and Mebaz, and invest in pin-code-level demand sensing to reduce markdowns.

risks.risk: Intensifying competition in the organised celebration wear market
risks.note: Management notes the market has increasing participation and competition and that other players falling under the same industry may increase competition, pressuring the Company's market-leading position and its no-discount stance on Manyavar.

The Company states it is affected by price volatility of its key raw materials and traded goods, with operating activities requiring a continuous supply of key material; the procurement department monitors price fluctuation to minimise exposure. The primary market risk to the Company is commodity price risk.

risks.risk: Credit risk concentrated in trade receivables from franchisees and distribution partners
risks.note: The maximum exposure to credit risk is primarily from trade receivables; the Company manages it through security deposits and bank guarantees from customers, credit approvals, credit limits and continuous monitoring of customer creditworthiness, with an impairment analysis performed at each reporting date.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange risk on overseas sales
risks.note: The Company operates in domestic and international markets and is exposed to foreign exchange risk through sales in overseas countries, principally USD with smaller CAD and GBP exposure; it holds forward contracts to mitigate the risk of changes in exchange rates.

risks.risk: Investment price risk on treasury portfolio
risks.note: The Company has invested in bonds, debentures and mutual funds which are susceptible to market price risk arising from changes in interest rates or market yields that may impact the return and value of such investments; it manages this by diversifying the portfolio.

risks.risk: Dependence on attracting and retaining skilled personnel
risks.note: The Company states its continued growth depends on the ability to attract, hire, train and retain skilled personnel — a structural exposure for a retail organisation whose in-store experience is a core differentiator.

risks.risk: Supply chain fragmentation in the apparel sector
risks.note: The Company notes the apparel sector supply chain is largely unorganised and fragmented and that it works with a diverse network of suppliers for raw materials, accessories and finished goods, creating dependence on jobbers and third-party vendors for quality and compliance.

The BRSR discloses a non-monetary regulatory instance concerning information not provided on the product label as required by law, which caused violation of Rule 9 of Legal Metrology Packaged Commodities Rule 2011.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Vedant Fashions Limited is the market leader in India's organised wedding and celebration wear segment, operating a portfolio of ethnic-wear brands through an EBO-led omni-channel network spanning 1.79 million square feet.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Vedant Fashions Limited, incorporated in 2002 and headquartered in Kolkata, is primarily engaged in manufacturing, trading and sale of readymade ethnic wear for men, women and kids, primarily in India, under the brand names Manyavar, Mohey, Mebaz, Twamev and Diwas. It caters to a diverse consumer base seeking ready-to-wear ethnic and occasion-based apparel and accessories for traditional, wedding, festive and celebration wear occasions. The Company follows an omni-channel retail strategy, serving customers through exclusive brand outlets (EBOs), multi-brand outlets (MBOs), large format stores (LFS) and digital platforms including its own website and leading third-party e-commerce portals.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Manyavar: core brand, 669 stores; Mohey: 8 standalone EBOs, higher ASP than Manyavar; Twamev: 8 standalone EBOs, highest revenue/sq ft, build-to-suit stores with 18-20 month lead time; Mebaz: focused on wedding/occasion wear; Diwas: digital-only, no physical stores planned; combined Manyavar-Mohey stores: all upgraded, no retrofitting possible

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Wearing Apparel & Accessories:** Manyavar, Mohey, Twamev, Diwas, Mebaz
- **Men's celebration wear:** Manyavar, Jodhpuri, footwear and men's accessories
- **Women's celebration wear:** Mohey, ready-to-wear and drape-led occasion wear, bags and clutches
- **Premium / luxury:** Twamev, EverAfter, The Drop, The Chord, Twilight Gala
- **Festive / Gen-Z:** Diwas
- **Regional (Southern market):** Mebaz

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India — 26 States and UTs, 240 cities and towns
- International stores across five countries: USA, UAE, UK, Canada and Australia
- Exclusive brand outlets (EBOs), the dominant channel
- Multi-brand outlets (MBOs) and large format stores (LFS)
- E-commerce — own brand websites and third-party marketplaces, including quick-commerce and B2B platforms
- Weddings, festive and celebration occasions for men, women and children

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: no explicit guidance, but confidence in sustained SSG momentum; margin: gross margin to remain ~65%+ despite 50-150 bps input cost inflation; order inflow: no specific guidance; capex/commissioning: no capex guidance, but Twamev EBOs have 18-20 month lead time for openings

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into high-throughput neighborhoods with 1,000 sq ft Manyavar kurta-only stores; potential for own quick-commerce app/dark hubs; untapped markets like South Bombay (Lower Parel+); new India tier-2 cities (e.g., Bhopal) with high rental friction

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's young demographic profile sustaining a large and aspirational consumer base with a strong propensity for fashion spending
- Accelerating urbanization expanding the addressable market and reshaping consumption patterns across Tier II and Tier III cities
- Rising participation of women in the workforce driving incremental demand for formal and occasion-specific apparel categories
- A gradual but decisive shift in consumer preference from unbranded to Ready-Made Garments (RMG), elevating market quality and value
- Deeper penetration of organized and branded players reinforcing consumer trust, standardizing sizing and quality expectations, and widening market formalization
- Expanding physical retail infrastructure alongside rapidly growing e-commerce adoption improving product accessibility and convenience
- Growing consumer awareness of fashion trends driven by social media influence and global exposure, shortening purchase cycles and elevating aspirational spending
- The increasing trend of multi-day wedding functions in India and higher spending per consumer, with demand driven not only by the immediate family of the bride and groom but also their close friends
- Frequent festivities in India driving the wedding and celebration wear category
- The E-commerce channel delivered robust growth during the year, while the relatively newer brands Twamev, Diwas and Mohey together recorded strong overall growth, strengthening overall brand portfolio performance
- Mohey's repositioning to a broader wedding wear brand has yielded encouraging early results, reflected in improved store footfalls and stronger floor conversions
- The Directors remain optimistic that the integrated and culturally attuned approach — spanning digital commerce, customer engagement, data analytics and AI-assisted tools — will continue to attract new customers, deepen loyalty and strengthen brand equity, supporting long-term growth

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin held at 65.7% (FY) despite 150 bps contraction — primarily due to GST rate normalization (not input inflation); fabric cost impact estimated at INR 1-1.5 per INR 100 MRP product, absorbed via SKU upgradation, not price hikes; no margin pressure from franchisees

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Historically paid 50% of profits as dividends; currently under internal review for policy update — no concrete decision yet; cash reserves available for inorganic plays but no active targets; acquisition interest exists but scale of targets too small to justify cost

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Vedant Fashions is an asset-light, franchisee-led retailer whose expansion is measured in retail footprint rather than plant capacity. As on March 31, FY26 the total retail footprint stood at 1.79 million sq. ft., and the Exclusive Brand Outlet (EBO) area — the dominant channel — spanned 669 stores (including SIS) in 252 cities and towns globally, of which the national EBO tally was 652 stores (including SIS) across 240 cities and towns in India. During the year the Company expanded brand presence by launching one exclusive brand outlet for the Twamev brand of 9,000 sq ft. Operationally the Company runs a centralized warehouse at Dhulagarh, Howrah, West Bengal, its registered and corporate office at Paridhan Garment Park, Kolkata, and fifteen company-operated retail outlets (five in Kolkata, two in Mumbai, eight in Bangalore); BRSR reports 16 plants and 1 office nationally and none internationally. International presence spans stores in five countries — USA, UAE, UK, Canada and Australia. Capacity-style investment during the year was directed at capability rather than manufacturing lines: full-scale activation of omnichannel fulfilment enabling online orders to be served from the store network, significant investment in brand-website UI/UX and AI-led product discovery, a performance-based allocation framework for logistics partners, scaling of AI-enabled camera infrastructure to an increased number of stores for footfall and conversion capture, organisation-wide deployment of Claude Enterprise, AI-driven intelligence embedded in real estate site selection and expansion decisions, and full automation of the in-store alteration workflow.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, disciplined, and long-term oriented; emphasis on SSG over store count; proud of marketing ROI (1B+ views for Made for Each Other); transparent on GST distortion; cautious on capex due to rental environment; open to acquisitions but no active pipeline

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market-leader in the Indian celebration wear segment with a diverse portfolio of brands catering to the aspirations of the entire family
- Large and growing Indian wedding and celebration wear market driven by increased customer spending on such wear
- Omni-channel network with the seamless integration of offline and online channels
- Differentiated business model combining the strengths of retailing with branded consumer play
- Technology-based strong supply chain and inventory replenishment systems driven by system-wide data analytics, strong processes, and long-standing vendor relationships
- Experienced and professional founder-led leadership team
- No end of season sales or discounts for the Manyavar brand
- Continued investment in capturing consumer taste preferences at a pin code level, enabling hyper-local demand sensing for sharper inventory planning and reduced markdowns
- The Company is debt-free, with negligible interest rate risk from financial liabilities

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: High rental inflation in tier-2 cities delaying store openings; reliance on wedding-centric demand; potential GST volatility; competition from regional players entering/exiting cycle; no quick-commerce integration due to third-party warehouse model

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: 1. 85% higher revenue/sq ft in new vs closed stores — indicates superior location selection, not just size; 2. Twamev’s 18-20 month lead time means current signings are for FY28/FY29 openings; 3. Diwas digital sales are scaling but inventory cannot be used by Zilo/Blinkit — company may need to build its own logistics; 4. 5-6% of retail area is underperforming — higher than typical 2-3%, signaling aggressive rationalization underway

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Shift the product architecture from category breadth to category depth, making offerings resonate with the evolving preferences of younger consumers — exemplified by reinventing the iconic Jodhpuri with comfort engineering and contemporary occasion-wear sensibilities to appeal to the Gen Z consumer
- Deepen regional relevance by developing occasion-specific and fabric-led offerings tailored to distinct cultural preferences and local traditions in key regional markets
- Reposition Mohey from a bridal wear brand to a broader wedding wear brand encompassing the full spectrum of celebration …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Marketing / brand assets] The deck details campaign activity including the Manyavar-Mohey 'Made for Each Other' campaign featuring Rashmika and Vijay, Vijay Devarakonda AI content, a Safari x Manyavar collaboration, Mohey influencer and stylist activations, Twamev's 'Truly You' / 'Product Is King' storytelling with Nupur Sanon, and Diwas festive content; the company has been Official Sponsor of 2 IPL teams and Official Indian Wear Partner of 3 IPL teams, and Celebration Wear Partner in Femina Miss India 2021.
- [Founder / heritage] Headquartered in Kolkata and incorporated in 2002 by Mr. Ravi Modi; the Manyavar brand started operations via a predecessor entity in 1999, with the first EBO in Bhubaneshwar.
- [Data vintage caveat] All market-leadership claims are sourced to the Crisil Report dated Sep-2021 as updated by an addendum dated December 2021, with the positioning statistics marked 'As of FY20 (latest available)'.
- [Metric definitions] The deck's 'Sales of Customers' / 'Retail Sales' is a distinct measure from Revenue from Operations - it comprises sales of the company's brands made by its EBOs, LFSs and online channel customers, plus sales made by the company to MBOs (including shop-in-shops) and certain lateral e-commerce platform customers at RSP - and must not be read as company revenue.
